source.title: Refund of Fees Procedure
source.note: The notes listed enrolment fees as policies.rmit.edu.au document id=147. That page requires RMIT staff SSO, so this public Enrolment Policy procedure is used instead for policy-based fee responsibilities.

chunks.text:
Source: Refund of Fees Procedure
Section: Section 1 - Context

(1) This procedure describes the rules for students seeking a refund of a credit balance in their student account and appealing a refund assessment decision.

Source: Refund of Fees Procedure
Section: Section 2 - Authority

(2) Authority for this document is established by the Enrolment Policy .

Source: Refund of Fees Procedure
Section: Section 3 - Scope

(3) This procedure applies to programs delivered by RMIT, and excludes programs delivered in partnership with other education providers.

(4) For students who also hold an enrolment with a partner institution, the policy and processes of the partner institution on refund of fees and remission of debt apply.

Source: Refund of Fees Procedure
Section: Section 4 - Procedure > Eligibility for a Refund

(5) The Approved Schedule of Fees and Charges outlines all fees that may be charged by RMIT for enrolment or other engagement with RMIT.

(6) Eligibility for a refund is determined with reference to the Approved Schedule of Fees and Charges .

(7) Where a student’s request for a refund of fees is denied the response will state the reasons for the decision and advise of the right to appeal.
1. Enrolled students considering appealing a refund decision are advised to contact the RMIT University Student Union (RUSU) Student Rights team for advice

Source: Refund of Fees Procedure
Section: Section 4 - Procedure > Eligibility for a Refund

(8) Students who wish to apply for a refund or appeal a refund decision must follow this procedure and the processes published by the University Secretary and Academic Registrar.

Source: Refund of Fees Procedure
Section: Section 4 - Procedure > Appeal of a Refund Decision

(9) The following students can appeal a decision not to refund fees and/or the refund amount for courses undertaken in the first six months of study at RMIT:
1. a commencing international student studying in Australia on student visa
2. a domestic student studying an ELICOS course offered by RMIT University Pathways (RMIT UP) in Australia.

Source: Refund of Fees Procedure
Section: Section 4 - Procedure > Appeal of a Refund Decision

(10) Students must have received written advice of the outcome of their refund application before lodging an appeal against a refund assessment decision.
1. International students may submit an appeal in writing, within 20 working days of the original refund outcome being sent to the student.
2. Appeals will be considered by the following: for RMIT Vietnam, Academic Registrar, or nominee for RMIT University, the Director, Global Student Recruitment.
3. Appeals are only considered if the student: provides evidence that the institution has made an error in process that has been a significant factor in the decision; and/or provides evidence that significant circumstances have not been taken into account; and/or provides new, relevant evidence that was not available at the time of the decision, which would have been a significant factor in the decision.
4. International students who are dissatisfied with the outcome of an appeal against a refund assessment decision may apply for external review of the decision by: Victorian Ombudsman for vocational eduation students the National Student Ombudsman for higher education students.
5. Domestic students who are dissatisfied with a decision not to refund fees may seek review of the decision by the: National Student Ombudsman for higher education students Victorian Ombudsman for vocational education students.

Source: Refund of Fees Procedure
Section: Section 5 - Resources

(11) Refer to the following documents which are established in accordance with this procedure:
1. Credit balance and refunds
2. Application for a refund form
3. Refunds for Commencing or Newly Enrolled International Students
